The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

Chip and the Backwards Queue

Chip set out two baskets for an Everybody Day guessing game. One held long leaves. One held round ones. Pick a leaf and make a shape. See if a friend can guess what you made! He made a neat line of stones for players to stand on.

Toad chose in a blink. Mouse chose in two blinks. At the front of the line, Snail looked into one basket. He looked into the other. “They are both so very… leafy,” he said.

Chip sighed. The line behind Snail wriggled like a worm. “I can pick one for you,” he offered. Snail pulled in his feelers. “I did rather come for the picking part.”

Chip tried standing in his own line. From the back, all he could see was Toad. From the middle, more Toad. The very first time he saw the baskets was the very instant he had to choose.

He carried one long leaf and one round leaf to the start of the line. “A little preview,” he said. Snail ran a feeler round each edge. “I like this. I still might take a while.”

Together they curved the stones into a loop beside the baskets. Anyone could go round for another look and join the picking spot when ready. Chip went twice. Now that he had time, he rather liked choosing.

Snail chose a long leaf. He worked behind a basket. “Guess what I have made.” Chip saw a long tip poking out. “A ladder?” Snail raised a round little crown. He had tucked the leaf’s tip through its own stem.

Chip drew the loop beside the two baskets on a paper leaf for the Welcome Tree. Snail wore his crown home. It had taken a little while to choose a leaf fit for a king.

Read together

Where would you stand if you wanted a little time to choose?
